To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coupling constants of the $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ channels to the $\Delta (1232)$ are $g_{\pi NN} = 14.1$ and $g_{\sigma NN} = 5.7$ respectively.
the $\pi NN(1440)$ and the $\sigma NN(1440) couplings are 2.6 and 2.2 times larger than the corresponding $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ couplings, respectively, and that they are both positive.
the $\pi NN$ coupling constant, as well as the $\sigma NN$ coupling constant are overestimated in the quark model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following points:   1.
the study of the NN* (1440) resonance in the framework of the quark model.
the study of the $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ couplings are in the right order of magnitude and that they are in the right direction, i.e., the $\sigma NN$ coupling constant has the same sign as the $\sigma NN^*$.
the $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ coupling constants are not well defined, but depend strongly on the particular model used for the $NN^*(1440)\to NN$ transition.

the quark model transition potentials yield $\pi NN^* (1440)$ and $ \sigma NN^* (1400)$ coupling constants which are compatible with the values obtained from the analysis of the $NN^*(1440)\to NN$ data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $\sigma NN^* \sim \sigma NN$ coupling constant is of the same order of magnitude as the $\pi NN \sim \pi NN$ one, while the $\pi NN*$ coupling constant is about 1/2 the $\pi NN$ one.
the $\sigma NN^* (1440)$ coupling constant is about 3 times larger than the $\pi NN*(1440)$ one.
we found a strong $\sigma NN^* \to NN$ decay mechanism which is in contradiction to the $\sigma NN$ coupling constant being zero.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quark model predicts that the $\pi NN$ and $\sigma NN$ coupling constants are very different from the values obtained in the standard $\pi NN$ model.
the $\pi NN(1440)$ and the $\sigma NN(1440$) couplings are both positive and that the $\sigma NN^* (1440)$ coupling constant is about twice the $\pi NN* (1440$) one, with a value of 0.5.

the $\pi NN$ coupling constant, as well as the $\pi NN(1535)$ and $\pi NN(1650)$ ones, is significantly overestimated by a naive quark model, whereas the $\pi NN*(1440)$ is in good agreement with the experimental value.
